role_and_stem.masculine: 7.1.98 supplies udātta ām before the designated strong endings. 7.1.99 supplies am in the vocative singular. 7.1.82 and the ending rules must be considered separately. The weak instrumental plural has d before bh in anaḍudbhiḥ.
role_and_stem.feminine: The Bhāṣya’s addition allows ām optionally when anaḍuh forms its feminine. Kāśikā invokes gaurādi and directly gives anaḍuhī and anaḍvāhī. These are alternatives at one case/number request; two schedules need not be counted as two positions.
role_and_stem.neuter: Prakriyāsarvasva at 7.4.48 explicitly gives svanaḍut, svanaḍuhī, svanaḍvāṃhi. Dual ī arises from the neuter dual ending; the plural has the strong augment and num. Vocative and accusative obey the indicated neuter relationships. The archive preserves final d and t spellings where the chosen nominal model lists both.

external_observation: The Zürich source’s anaḷútsu has ḷ where the ordinary table has ḍ. Both other tokens agree in letters after removing accent and visibly bear acute on the strong ā. No written classical ending was multiplied by the number of Vedic tokens.
